First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int \operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,\text{d}t,-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
